## Claims
- [source-backed] In \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(q=n-r\), the Schur classes \(\bar s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\) form the quotient Schur basis. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- [source-backed] The Hopf antipode satisfies \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\), and hence \(\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(-1)^{|\alpha|}c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\nu}s_{\alpha'}s_\beta=0\) for \(\nu\ne\varnothing\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-736]
- [proved] For every \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
  \[
  [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
  =(-1)^{|\rho|}
  [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b})}]
  \quad\text{in }Q:=J_v/A_+J_v .
  \tag{SC}
  \]
- [computed] For \((i,j,a,b)=(2,3,2,2)\), (SC) gives
  \[
  [222]=[222],\ [2221]=-[322],\ [2222]=[332],\
  [22211]=[422],\ [22221]=-[432],\ [22222]=[442],
  \]
  matching complete integral relation-lattice computations; the degree blocks have determinants \(1,-1,-1,-1,1\). [artifact b525c6b69aec42dfda85ba9b819a6a11265e17552b8c81c742e5f276ef669fc4]

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\). Assume
\[
a,j,i,b\ge0,\qquad a+j\le r,\qquad a+i\le q,\qquad b\le i,j.
\]
Write \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\), padding by zeroes, and define
\[
\rho'_t=\#\{u: \rho_u\ge t\}\quad(1\le t\le b).
\]
Thus \(\rho'\subseteq a^b\). Conventions are
\[
(i^j,\rho)=(\underbrace{i,\ldots,i}_{j},\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a),
\]
and
\[
R_\rho=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,
\underbrace{i,\ldots,i}_{j-b}).
\]
Both are partitions in \(q^r\): the first has width at most \(i\) and length at most \(j+a\); the second has width at most \(i+a\) and length \(j\).

Let \(\mathcal J\subseteq\Lambda\) be generated by
\[
L_\lambda:=s_{(i^j,\lambda)}\qquad(\lambda\subseteq b^a).
\]
The bordered Jacobi--Trudi/antipode reduction is
\[
s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho}
 \in
 \sum_{\lambda\subsetneq\rho}
 \Lambda_{|\rho|-|\lambda|}\,s_{(i^j,\lambda)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Here every coefficient has strictly positive degree. To verify (1), apply the Hopf identity in the second claim to \(s_\rho\), use \(S(s_\mu)=(-1)^{|\mu|}s_{\mu'}\), and attach the \(i\times j\) rectangle to the northwest. In the resulting bordered Jacobi--Trudi expansion, the two boundary coproduct terms are respectively \(s_{(i^j,\rho)}\) and \((-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho}\); every remaining term has a proper lower tail \(\lambda\subsetneq\rho\) and a positive-degree Schur factor. The subtraction in the \(\mathrm{CP}\)-term contributes the displayed sign.

Map (1) to \(A\). Since the accepted generating family \(\{\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)}:\lambda\subseteq b^a\}\) generates \(J_v\), its right side lies in \(A_+J_v\). Its image in \(Q\) is therefore zero, proving (SC).

If \(a=0\), then \(\rho=\varnothing\), \(\rho'=0^b\), and (SC) is \([\bar s_{i^j}]=[\bar s_{i^j}]\). If \(b=0\), the same conclusion holds. Thus all boundary cases are included.
